title: Gavin Newsom claims he ‘didn’t even know’ detail about 5,000-bottle wine cellar at his $7.5M home
text:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom and wife Jennifer Siebel Newsom are selling their $7.5 million Sacramento-area residence  — yet the governor claims he was barely aware of a detail of one of the home’s key amenities.

At a press conference, the winemaker-turned-pol was put on the spot about whether he even filled the home’s massive 5,000-bottle wine cellar.

“Are you serious? Really?” the Democrat asked, stunned.

“No, I never filled it. I didn’t even know I had that much.”

“I literally didn’t even know,” the governor added, claiming he only found out that 5,000-figure detail about his own home from the news.

“By the way, I put books in there,” Newsom claimed.

“There’s no wine there, it’s books,” he went on, suggesting they were his “only inheritance” from his father, former judge and Gordon Getty consigliere William Newsom.

California’s first couple listed the home for $7.5 million Tuesday — double what they paid for it eight years ago, according to its Zillow real estate listing.

The secluded home features a “personal wellness oasis,” a resort-style pool, full-size tennis court, and a “private casita” in addition to the sprawling basement booze cave, according to a property description.

Newsom is winding down his time in the California capitol as he preps an expected White House run. Outside of Sacramento, the couple purchased a $9 million home in Marin County in 2024.

Photos of the wine cellar show a luxurious, open area with seating and rows of shelves locked behind a glass door. There appear to be books stacked inside the walls along with bottles of wine.

The Newsoms earned between $1.7 million and $2 million annually between 2022 and 2024, according to tax returns released last month.

Much of the family’s income comes from Newsom’s stakes in a lucrative wine and hospitality business he founded off the back of his connections to one of California’s wealthiest families, the Getty oil clan.

The powerful couple’s finances came under scrutiny this year after the governor revealed that his family and associates were under investigation by federal law enforcement, which Newsom described as a political hit job.
